title: Mutual information is bounded by the entropy of either variable
statement:
Let $X \colon \Omega \to S$ and $Y \colon \Omega \to T$ be measurable random variables, each taking only finitely many values, defined on a space $\Omega$ equipped with a measure $\mu$ that is either the zero measure or a probability measure. Writing $H[Y;\mu]$ for the Shannon entropy of $Y$ and $I[X:Y;\mu]$ for the mutual information between $X$ and $Y$, one has
\[
  I[X:Y;\mu] \;\le\; H[Y;\mu].
\]
hypotheses_covered: mu is zero or a probability measure
replaced:
For measurable $X$ and $Y$ under a zero-or-probability measure $\mu$ with finite ranges,
\[
  I[X : Y;\mu] \;\le\; H[Y;\mu].
\]
